SIKAFLOOR®-160: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikafloor®-160, April 2023, Version 05.04 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/7/sikafloor_-160.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikafloor®-160 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 05.04).
1.2 Product description. Sikafloor®-160 is an economic, two part, low viscosity epoxy resin. "Total solid epoxy composition according to the test method Deutsche Bauchemie e.V. (German Association for construction chemicals)"
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikafloor®-160 may only be used by experienced professionals.
    - For priming concrete substrates, cement screeds and epoxy mortars
    - For low to medium absorbent substrates
    - Primer for a varity of Sikafloor MultiDur and MultiFlex flooring systems
    - Binder for levelling mortars and mortar screeds
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.15.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikafloor®-160
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: 2-part epoxy primer, levelling mortar, intermediate layer and mortar screed
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer - LEED Rating. Sikafloor®-160 conforms to the requirements of LEED EQ Credit 4.2: Low-Emitting Materials: Paints & Coatings SCAQMD Method 304-91 VOC Content < 100 g/l
2.3 Approvals / certificates.
    - Epoxy primer, levelling mortar and mortar screed according to EN 1504-2: 2004 and EN 13813:2002, DoP 02 08 01 02 050 0 000021 1008, certified by Factory Production Control Body No. 0921 and provided with the CE-mark.
    - “Products and systems for the protection and repair of concrete structures–Test method – Compatibility on wet concrete when exposed to the effects of humidity from the rear” according to the DIN EN 13578:2004.Proof statement P 9400-E
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-2: 2004: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 13813:2002: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - DIN EN 13578:2004: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - DIN EN ISO 2811-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.2).
    - DIN 53 505: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore D Hardness (p.2).
    - EN13892-2: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile strength in flexure (p.2).
    - ISO 4624: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Low viscosity
    - Good penetration
    - Excellent bond strength
    - Easy application
    - Short waiting times
    - Multi-purpose
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Epoxy
2.7 Appearance and colour.
    | Resin - part A | brownish-transparent, liquid |
    | Hardener - part B | transparent, liquid |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
2.8 Density.
    | Part A | ~ 1.13 kg/l |
    | Part B | ~ 1.02 kg/l |
    | Mixed Resin | ~ 1.10 kg/l |
    | All density values at +23°C |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
2.9 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Solid content by mass: ~100 %
    - Solid content by volume: ~100 %
    - Shore D Hardness: ~76 (7 days / +23°C) (DIN 53 505)
    - Compressive strength: Mortar Screed: >35 N/mm² (28 days / +23°C / 50 % r.h.) (EN13892-2)
    - Tensile strength in flexure: Mortar Screed: ~15 N/mm² (28 days / +23°C / 50 % r.h.) (EN13892-2)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: > 1.5 N/mm² (failure in concrete) (ISO 4624)
2.10 Temperature resistance.
    | Exposure* | Dry heat |
    | Permanent | +50°C |
    | Short-term max. 7 d | +80°C |
    | Short-term max. 12 h | +100°C |
    Short-term moist/wet heat* up to +80°C where exposure is only occasional (steam cleaning etc.).
    Note printed: *No simultaneous chemical and mechanical exposure and only in combination with Sikafloor® systems as a broadcast system with approx. 3 - 4 mm thickness.
2.11 Systems. Primer
    | Low / medium porosity concrete | 1 - 2 x Sikafloor®-160 |
    | Levelling mortar fine (surface roughness < 1 mm) |
    | Primer | 1 - 2 x Sikafloor®-160 |
    | Levelling mortar | 1 x Sikafloor®-160 + quartz sand (0.1 |
    | - 0.3 mm) |
    | Levelling mortar medium (surface roughness up to 2 mm) |
    | Primer | 1-2 x Sikafloor®-160 |
    | Levelling mortar | 1 x Sikafloor®-160 + quartz sand (0.1 |
    | - 0.3 mm) |
    | Intermediate layer (self-smoothing 1.5 to 3 mm) |
    | Primer | 1 x Sikafloor®-160 |
    | Levelling mortar | 1 x Sikafloor®-160 + quartz sand (0.1 |
    | - 0.3 mm) |
    | Epoxy screed (15 - 70 mm layer thickness) / repair mortar |
    | Primer | 1-2 x Sikafloor®-160 |
    | Bonding bridge | 1 x Sikafloor®-160 |
    | Screed | 1 x Sikafloor®-160 + suitable sand |
    | mixture |
    | In practice the following sand mixtures proved to be suitable (grain size distribution for layer thicknesses of 15 - 70 mm): |
    | 25 pbw quartz sand 0.1 - 0.5 mm |
    | 25 pbw quartz sand 0.4 - 0.7 mm |
    | 25 pbw quartz sand 0.7 - 1.2 mm |
    | 25 pbw quartz sand 2 - 4 mm |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
    Note: The largest grain size should be a maximum 1/3 of the finished layer thickness. Dependent on the grain shape and application temperatures, the aggregates and the most suitable mix should be selected.
2.12 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: The packaging must be stored properly in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5°C and +30°C.
2.13 Packaging.
    | Part A | 7.1   kg containers |
    | Part B | 4.0   kg containers |
    | Part A+B | 11.1 kg ready to mix units |
    | Part A | 20 KG drums |
    | Part B | 20 KG drums |

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 05.04) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment.
    - The concrete substrate must be sound and of sufficient compressive strength (minimum 25 N/mm²) with a minimum pull off strength of 1.5 N/mm².
    - The substrate must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings and surface treatments, etc.
    - Concrete substrates must be prepared mechanically using abrasive blast cleaning or scarifying equipment to remove cement laitance and achieve an open textured surface.
    - Weak concrete must be removed and surface defects such as blow holes and voids must be fully exposed.
    - Repairs to the substrate, filling of blowholes/voids and surface levelling must be carried out using appropriate products from the Sikafloor®, Sikadur® and Sikagard® range of materials.
    - All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by brush or vacuum.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 05.04) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Part A : Part B = 64 : 36 (by weight) 1.6:1 (by volume)
4.3 Consumption.
    | Coating System | Product | Consumption |
    | Priming | 1 - 2 x Sikafloor®-160 | 1 - 2 x 0.25 - 0.50 kg/m² |
    | Levelling mortar fine | 1 pbw Sikafloor®-160 + | 1.4 kg/m²/mm |
    | (surface roughness < 1 | 0.5 pbw quartz sand |
    | mm) | (0.1 - 0.3 mm) |
    | Levelling mortar medi- | 1 pbw Sikafloor®-160 + | 1.6 kg/m²/mm) |
    | um (surface roughness | 1 pbw quartz sand (0.1 - |
    | up to 2 mm) | 0.3 mm) |
    | Intermediate layer (self- | 1 pbw Sikafloor®-160 + | 1.6 kg/m²/mm |
    | smoothing 1.5 to 3 mm) | 1 pbw quartz sand (0.1 - |
    | 0.3 mm) |
    | + optional broadcast | ~ 4.0 kg/m² |
    | quartz sand 0.4 – 0.7 mm |
    | Bonding bridge | 1 - 2 x Sikafloor®-160 | 1- 2 x 0.3 - 0.5 kg/m² |
    | Epoxy screed (15 - 20 | 1 pbw Sikafloor®-160 + | 2.2 kg/m²/mm |
    | mm layer thickness ) / | 8 pbw quartz sand |
    | Repair Mortar |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Note printed: Note: These figures are theoretical and do not allow for any additional material required due to surface porosity, surface profile, variations in level or wastage etc.
4.4 Pot Life.
    | Temperature | Time |
    | +10°C | ~50 minutes |
    | +20°C | ~25 minutes |
    | +30°C | ~15 minutes |
4.5 Curing time. Before applying solvent free products on Sikafloor®-160 allow:
    | Substrate temperature | Minimum | Maximum |
    | +10°C | 24 hours | 4 days |
    | +20°C | 12 hours | 2 days |
    | +30°C | 8 hours | 24 hours |
    | Before applying solvent containing products on Sikafloor®-160 allow: |
    | Substrate temperature | Minimum | Maximum |
    | +10°C | 36 hours | 6 days |
    | +20°C | 24 hours | 4 days |
    | +30°C | 16 hours | 2 days |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions particularly temperature and relative humidity.
4.6 Mixing. Prior to mixing, stir part A mechanically. When all of part B has been added to part A, mix continuously for 3 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved. When parts A and B have been mixed, add the quartz sand and if required the Extender T and mix for a further 2 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved. To ensure thorough mixing pour materials into another container and mix again to achieve a consistent mix. Over mixing must be avoided to minimise air entrainment.
4.7 Mixing - Mixing Tools. Sikafloor®-160 must be thoroughly mixed using a low speed electric stirrer (300 - 400 rpm) or other suitable equipment. For the preparation of mortars use a forced action mixer of rotating pan, paddle or trough type. Free fall mixers should not be used.
4.8 Application. Prior to application, confirm substrate moisture content, relative air humidity and dew point. If > 4% pbw moisture content, Sikafloor® EpoCem® may be applied as a T.M.B. (temporary moisture barrier) system.
4.9 Application - Primer. Make sure a continuous, pore free coat covers the substrate. If necessary, apply two priming coats. Apply Sikafloor®-160 by brush, roller or squeegee. Preferred application is by using a squeegee and then backrolling crosswise.
4.10 Application - Levelling mortar. Rough surfaces need to be levelled first. Apply the levelling mortar by squeegee/trowel to the required thickness.
4.11 Application - Intermediate layer. Sikafloor®-160 is poured, spread evenly by means of a serrated trowel. Roll immediately in two directions with spiked roller to ensure even thickness and if required broadcast with quartz sand, after about 15 minutes (at +20°C) but before 30 minutes (at+20°C), at first lightly and then to excess.
4.12 Application - Bonding bridge. Apply Sikafloor®-160 by brush, roller or squeegee. Preferred application is by using a squeegee and then backrolling crosswise.
4.13 Application - Epoxy screed / repair mortar. Apply the mortar screed evenly on the still “tacky” bonding bridge, using levelling battens and screed rails as necessary. After a short waiting time compact and smoothen the mortar with a trowel or Teflon coated power float (usually 20 - 90 rpm).
4.14 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Thinner C immediately after use. Hardened and/or cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.15 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Do not apply Sikafloor®-160 on substrates with rising moisture.
    - Freshly applied Sikafloor®-160 should be protected from damp, condensation and water for at least 24 hours.
    - Sikafloor®-160 mortar screed is not suitable for frequent or permanent contact with water unless sealed.
    - Practical trials should be carried out for mortar mixes to assess suitable aggregate grain size distribution.
    - For external applications, apply on a falling temperature. If applied during rising temperatures “pin holing” may occur from rising air.
    - These pinholes can be closed after a soft grinding by applying a scratch coat of Sikafloor-161 mixed with approx. 3 % of Extender T.
    - The incorrect assessment and treatment of cracks may lead to a reduced service life and reflective cracking.
    - Under certain conditions, underfloor heating or high ambient temperatures combined with high point loading, may lead to imprints in the resin.
    - If heating is required do not use gas, oil, paraffin or other fossil fuel heaters, these produce large quantities of both CO2 and H2O water vapour, which may adversely affect the finish. For heating use only electric powered warm air blower systems.
    - Static Cracks: prefill and level with Sikadur® or Sikafloor® epoxy resin
    - Dynamic cracks: to be assessed and if necessary apply a stripe coat of elastomeric material or design as a movement joint
    Construction joints require pre-treatment. Treat as follows:
4.16 Limitations and important considerations - Recommended supplier of tools. PPW-Polyplan-Werkzeuge GmbH, Phone: +49 40/5597260, www.polyplan.com
4.17 Further information.
    - Substrate quality & Preparation
    - Please refer to Sika Method Statement: “EVALUATION AND PREPARATION OF SURFACES FOR FLOORING SYSTEMS”.
    - Application instructions
    - Please refer to Sika Method Statement: “MIXING & APPLICATION OF FLOORING SYSTEMS”.
    - Maintenance
    - Please refer to “Sikafloor®- CLEANING REGIME”.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +10°C min. / +30°C max.
5.3 Relative air humidity. 80 % r.h. max.
5.4 Dew point. Beware of condensation! The substrate and uncured floor must be at least 3°C above dew point to reduce the risk of condensation or blooming on the floor finish. Note: Low temperatures and high humidity conditions increase the probability of blooming.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +10°C min. / +30°C max.
5.6 Substrate moisture content. Maximum 4% when measures using Sika® - Tramex meter ( at the time of application). Please note that the moisture content must be < 4 % pbw when using the CM measurement or Oven-dry-method. No rising moisture according to ASTM (Polyethylene-sheet).
5.7 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.15):
    - Do not apply Sikafloor®-160 on substrates with rising moisture.
    - For external applications, apply on a falling temperature. If applied during rising temperatures “pin holing” may occur from rising air.
    - Under certain conditions, underfloor heating or high ambient temperatures combined with high point loading, may lead to imprints in the resin.
5.8 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: Part A | ~ 1.13 kg/l; Part B | ~ 1.02 kg/l; Mixed Resin | ~ 1.10 kg/l; All density values at +23°C (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
    - Shore D Hardness: ~76 (7 days / +23°C) (DIN 53 505)
    - Compressive strength: Mortar Screed: >35 N/mm² (28 days / +23°C / 50 % r.h.) (EN13892-2)
    - Tensile strength in flexure: Mortar Screed: ~15 N/mm² (28 days / +23°C / 50 % r.h.) (EN13892-2)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: > 1.5 N/mm² (failure in concrete) (ISO 4624)
5.9 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.10 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikafloor®-160, April 2023, Version 05.04, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/7/sikafloor_-160.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikafloor 160/161/264 Part B, version 09/09/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/z/SDS%20Sikafloor%20-%20160-161-264%20Part%20B%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikafloor - 160-264 Part B, version 09/09/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/p/SDS%20Sikafloor%20-%20160-264%20Part%20B%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-160 Part A, version 13/09/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/i/sds-sikafloor-160parta.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-160/161/263 SL/264 Part B, version 07/10/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/q/sds-sikafloor-160161263sl264partb.pdf
    - Brochure: SikaFloor: Resin Flooring Solutions, version 08/11/2023, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/l/Sikafloor%20Resin%20BROCHURE%202023%20FIN%20DIGI.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-160/264 Part B, https://aus.sika.com/dms/getdocument.get/62143287-7c52-4609-9941-9c7fda1e9e69_au01/sds-sikafloor-160264partb.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-160/161/264 Part B, https://aus.sika.com/dms/getdocument.get/ba512ba4-21df-492b-8dc4-5b3560792eec_au01/sds-sikafloor-160161264partb.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-160/161/263 SL/264/264 T Part B, https://aus.sika.com/dms/getdocument.get/c06685f3-64a2-4ad0-9964-236c80db9a1d_au01/sds-sikafloor-160161263sl264264tpartb.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
